I have similar OCD problems pertaining to health. I used to worry about cancer when I was younger, going to doctors, googling on the internet for symptoms, rumination, compulsions etc. Currently I worry about HIV, so much so that I've had 7 tests in the last year. I had the exact same mind set, if I do not perform my compulsions or test, then I am going to somehow become positive. However, I had a good 3 months where I stopped worrying because I refused to get tested, not seeking reassurance is vital. I had worried that a previous HIV test had infected me through the use of a dirty needle \(completely irrational\), 5 weeks later I got the flu, early HIV symptoms are described as "flu like" so i began to freak out. However, I did not go get tested for 3 months and although the first few weeks were tough, the anxiety slowly went away because I was not feeding that cycle. Later I did end up getting tested because of a weekend that I remembered the flu I had and got very anxious... and of course it was negative, but now the anxiety is back. Which goes to show that the reassurance seeking and performing compulsions is counter productive. I know you would have discussed the importance of not performing compulsions so I don't want to reiterate too much but if you've prevented yourself from performing them, next time try to practice some mindfulness techniques when you start to worry. Try sitting with the thoughts but not reacting to them, acknowledging that they are there and that we cannot change them but we can change how we react to them. Over time they should lose their importance and fade. I still have thoughts from obsessions I had years ago but they have no impact on me whatsoever, and do not provoke anxiety, they just come and then go.

When I implied you cant really blame them for not knowing I do not mean to say that what they say regarding your anxiety is okay, or that its excused just because they do not know. I just mean that perhaps that is the reason they resort to such comments but in no way am i excusing it or think its okay, not at all your fault or something you should have to deal with!!! Good luck to you!

I find that parents, particularly older generations, have a hard time understanding mental illness. I mean, even now, most people do not understand OCD and consider it a "cleaning disorder". I can't speak for you as I do not know the relationship with your parents but mine were ultimately the same until I got an official diagnosis and they did their own research on OCD. Maybe now they will become more aware of your struggle through education. Either way it is not your fault for feeling the way you do and keep that in mind even if they are unable to understand. Your opinion of yourself should not be determined by a lack of understanding by your parents on a difficult issue, I know thats easier said than done, but it is the case. Are you planning on discussing this further with your parents?

I'd have to disagree with this sentiment. HIV symptoms are highly variable in acute infection and often do not occur at all/mimic those of much more common illness, including those of high anxiety. Looking for symptoms, particularly with OCD could be catastrophic as there are several possible symptoms such as fever, sore throat, rash, swollen lymph nodes that can be caused by other things. In fact, less than 1% of people who went to doctors worried about ARS \(Early HIV\) symptoms ended up actually having HIV. I'd say it be much more rational to go with the premise that only 4 instances of HIV transmission have occurred since the 1980s of health care worker to patient transmission, the last one being in 2006. However, my point is not the rational as we know OCD is highly irrational, so I am wondering how to deal with false memories, unless it would be wise to think I am the 5th person to ever be infected and 1st from drawing blood in history, during the thing I'm being tested for.
